# Research log

## 2026-10-12T13:40:23+00:00 — Initiate NVIDIA Q3 FY27 Data Center at $103bn; calendar 2026 $374.62bn versus $372bn street

Run: 2b53c59e74bc4e94862379a66c944e1c. Item: agent-task-13aeebc1, scheduled internal coverage initiation.

I initiate coverage with calendar 2026 capex of $682.5bn, $15bn above the October 5 street: Microsoft $150bn cash PP&E, Alphabet $180bn purchases, Amazon $215bn gross purchases, and Meta $137.5bn including finance-lease principal. First-half spending supports modest second-half acceleration; Meta stays at its latest guide midpoint [msft-2026-07-29-release] [googl-2026-07-22-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release] [meta-2026-07-29-release].

My unreported NVIDIA Q3 FY27 Data Center estimate is $103bn, expected November 18, 2026; the date is unconfirmed. I assume $110.5bn total revenue, 2.3% above guidance, less $7.5bn Edge. Recent total-revenue beats were larger. The revised annual base is $374.62bn versus $372bn street, requiring $129.86bn Q4; my own Q4 view is $128bn. I narrow the starting tails because their quarterly bridges were implausible [nvda-2026-08-26-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-cfo].

AMD is $14.00bn versus $14bn street: combined EPYC/Instinct disclosure cannot establish a GPU-only variant. Named Helios deployments challenge the delay premise; AWS margin expansion challenges its short premise. Watch late-October capex and November shipment conversion [amd-2026-08-04-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release] [street-oct2026].

Position read: NVIDIA/MSFT longs strengthen; AMD/AMZN shorts weaken; Alphabet’s TPU-cost thesis remains untested. NVIDIA’s street gap moves from -$5.62bn to +$2.62bn, AMD from +$1.22bn to $0.00bn; MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN capex gaps each rise $5bn.

Investigation: What NVIDIA Q3 FY27 Data Center estimate and calendar 2026 scenario range are consistent with reported quarters, total-revenue guidance and hyperscaler capex tracking? Status: partially answered.

Finding: Record Q3 Data Center $103bn: total $110.5bn less Edge $7.5bn, a smaller guide beat than recent quarters. Exact reported calendar contribution is $185.0403bn; own Q4 $128bn gives calendar $373.37bn, close to the revised top-down $374.62bn and required Q4 $129.86bn. Tighten initial implausible tails to NVIDIA $351.34-394.78bn. Recast Hyperscale includes consumer internet and other public clouds; its 54.7% Q2 share does not identify Big Four concentration. AMD GPU-only revenue remains unresolved; retain near-street $14.00bn. IR fetches did not confirm the expected November 18 date, and Microsoft/Alphabet transcript URLs returned 404. Legacy '2024' benchmark labels conflict with the explicit calendar-2026 street source; retain benchmark numbers and use the stated 2026 model horizon.

Checks: Read all six companies' available 2026 results and prior-quarter language. Microsoft cash PP&E rose 29.876 (December 2025 quarter) → 30.876 → 35.802; calendar H1 is 66.678, distinct from fiscal-year 115.948. Alphabet Q1/Q2 purchases are 35.674/44.924 versus February's 175–185 calendar guide. Meta guide rose 115–135 → 125–145 → 130–145, with component prices/future buildings part of the April raise. Amazon gross purchases rose 44.203 → 54.208, with net capex and original “about 200” guide not treated as the same measure. AMD segment progression 5.380 → 5.775 → 6.718 combines EPYC and Instinct and cannot establish GPU-only revenue. NVIDIA Q1 cohort was recast; avoid falsely inferring an organic increase from unrecast Q1's 50.3% to Q2's 54.7%.

Changed: MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN each +5bn; META held. Nine driver changes recorded via update_model; base NVIDIA mix/split/concentration held. Bear/base/bull NVIDIA 351.34/374.62/394.78; AMD 11.48/14.00/17.75. All changed driver sizes are judgment; AMD's base is a consensus anchor rather than an unsupported variant. Filing-exact prior Q4/Q1/Q2 and Q3 estimate plus own Q4 view saved via update_quarters. See analysis/2026-10-12-initiation.json for the exact decision and contiguous quotations.

Primary fetches: web-128f212df3 (Microsoft July release, confirming the corpus), web-714aaaf1ed (NVIDIA event page, no date exposed), web-f5106e7c08 (Alphabet IR landing page, no guidance exposed), web-955f652668 (NVIDIA news index, no earnings date exposed). Microsoft FY26 Q4 transcript and Alphabet Q2 earnings-event URLs returned 404; NVIDIA's alternate press-release-index URL also returned 404. No unsupported call guidance or confirmed date inferred.

Verification: analysis/check_initiation.py validates every decision quotation against its source file, all changed/saved inputs, filing-exact quarters and preserved output formulas. compute with explicit proposed inputs agrees with the saved top-down build. compute without overrides and update_quarters diagnostics reference the pre-decision current_view snapshot (366.38 base); the saved formulas/inputs instead imply Q4 129.8645. Application recalculation remains authoritative; no output numbers were typed over formulas. A no-input Change log correction records that the first reason's -32.45bn starting-bear Q4 was a typo; correct value is approximately -32.81bn.

Open: H2 cash capex/lease mix; accelerator versus building/pricing content; true Big Four concentration; actual NVIDIA Q3 and Q4 guide; AMD recognized GPU-only revenue/customer conversion; 2027 guides and AWS margin persistence. See notes/open-questions.md for answer sources and timing.

Next: Can AMD's latest earnings-call material quantify recognized Instinct revenue and separate 2026 Meta/Azure Helios shipments from multiyear deployment plans?

Attention: Are the AMD deployment-delay and Amazon margin-compression short premises still valid after named Helios deployments and Q2 AWS margin expansion? Rule 1: contrary evidence on held names; AMD base falls 8.0%, and NVIDIA crosses above street.

Position read: NVIDIA/MSFT longs strengthen; AMD/AMZN shorts weaken; Alphabet's TPU-cost thesis remains untested; Meta's capex stays at street. NVIDIA gap -5.62 → +2.62, AMD +1.22 → approximately zero; MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN capex gaps each +5bn. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.

## 2026-10-12T13:53:37+00:00 — Custom-order check trims NVIDIA bull to $391.79bn; base $374.62bn and Q3 $103bn held

Run: 8e4d912a97c74f539e96d685fece12f2. Item: channel-oct2026, synthetic material channel check.

The October 1–8 synthetic check reports larger 2027 orders from three ODM/OEM respondents, rising custom-accelerator order share at two unnamed clouds, and one planner whose deployment pace depends on power [channel-oct2026]. I compared it with AWS’s February production disclosures and April/July Trainium commitments. Those primary sources independently support custom adoption; they do not verify the unnamed clouds or incremental dollar shares [amzn-2026-02-05-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release].

This is a distinct document/interview channel, but respondent independence and order overlap remain unverified. I count one check, not eight corroborations. I halve NVIDIA’s optional bull capture premium over the 65% base: 66% becomes 65.5%, a judgment haircut that lowers calendar 2026 bull revenue $2.99bn to $391.79bn. The check mainly concerns 2027; it changes my confidence in favorable share persistence, not measured 2026 share.

Power readiness could stage deployment despite larger orders, but no dated slip is established. Stable neocloud lead times are not evidence of deterioration. I therefore retain $682.5bn capex, $103bn Q3 Data Center, own Q4 $128bn and AMD base $14.00bn. I partly disagree with the vendor’s “share, not volume” conclusion: energized volume also depends on power.

NVIDIA’s long capture thesis weakens slightly in the upside; its base street gap stays +$2.62bn (+0.70%), while the bull gap narrows from +$22.78bn to +$19.79bn.

Investigation: Does this check add independent evidence of custom silicon taking incremental cloud accelerator spending, and do power constraints shift deployment timing despite larger 2027 orders? Status: partially answered.

Finding: The report is a distinct source family claiming fresh October interviews and adds an apparently incremental order-mix observation; anonymous respondents and order overlap prevent verifying independence. No earlier eligible channel check was found. Prior AWS primary disclosures independently establish Trainium deployment and 2027 capacity commitments, but do not validate the two unnamed clouds or incremental dollar share. Power can constrain energized deployment despite larger orders, as one 2027 planner reports; no dated shipment, acceptance or revenue slip is established. Stable neocloud lead times provide no evidence of deterioration. Conditionally, new orders placed October 1–8 at 20–30 weeks would fall February 18–May 6, 2027; this is arithmetic, not a disclosed delivery schedule. Cut only NVIDIA bull share 0.5 point as a persistence-confidence haircut; hold 2026 base/capex, Q3 $103bn, own Q4 $128bn and AMD. Public confirmation of power timing remains unresolved; Microsoft annual-report fetch returned 404.

What arrived: Supply Chain Signals' October 1–8 eight-person sample. Three ODM/OEM managers report larger 2027 rack orders; two unspecified respondents report rising custom share at two unnamed Big Four clouds; one planner identifies power as the 2027 pacing constraint; neocloud procurement leads report stable NVIDIA 20–30 week lead times and improving AMD rack availability. These are vendor-reported observations, not verified customer disclosures [channel-oct2026].

What I checked: Earlier eligible channel reports were absent in the source list/search. Compared with Amazon February Trainium3 production and Trainium4 2027 timing, April chip-count mix/OpenAI 2027 Trainium ramp, July multi-gigawatt commitments, NVIDIA August Rubin deployments and Q3 total guide, and AMD August Azure Helios/mixed CPU-GPU revenue. AWS primary disclosures support direction independently but do not validate the anonymous clouds, dollars or respondents. Chip counts and the broader CPU/custom-chip revenue business are not accelerator spending share. Date-filtered searches were used for prior disclosures; a separate unfiltered search included live-labelled channel documents. Microsoft annual-report URL https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar26/index.html returned 404, leaving operational power timing unresolved.

Demand versus timing: Larger orders support 2027 demand intentions, without quantified dollars or delivery dates. A power constraint can stage energization despite intact orders. The vendor's “share, not volume” opinion overlooks commissioned capacity. Stable lead times do not demonstrate new delay. Conditional October 1–8 new orders plus 20–30 weeks give February 18–May 6, 2027; this is illustrative arithmetic, not a procurement forecast or proof of customer acceptance timing.

Changed: Only Inputs!D12, NVIDIA bull spend share 66%→65.5%. Half the optional 1-point premium over 65% base is removed as judgment under forward, anonymous evidence. NVIDIA bull 394.7764→391.7857 (-2.9907, -0.76%); its street gap 22.78→19.79. At conditional bull Q3 108, required Q4 is now 148.118 (+37.1%), versus 152.604 previously. Base 374.6167, required base Q4 129.8645, own Q4 128, recorded Q3 103, capex 682.5 and all AMD inputs remain held. No inference of a measured 2026 share loss, a guide change or an established 2026 slip.

Verification: update_model records the single input change. analysis/channel_update.py validates every exact contiguous decision quote, all changed/held input cells, preserved reported quarter sources and output formulas. analysis/2026-10-12-channel-sensitivity.json records before/after mathematics and the conditional lead-time window. No output formula was overwritten.

Open: Respondent independence/order overlap; anonymous customer identity and custom units-versus-dollar share; specific power-ready/acceptance/deployment dates; comparable prior lead-time baseline. Existing capex, concentration, NVIDIA actuals, AMD GPU and 2027 guide questions are carried forward in notes/open-questions.md.

Next: Which primary hyperscaler disclosures give power-ready dates and shipment/acceptance schedules that could validate or refute the channel's 2027 deployment constraint?

Attention: none. Base remains above street; the only forecast move is a 0.76% bull reduction. The report weakens the upside capture leg without making the overall NVIDIA base contrary to the held long. Previously recorded AMD/Amazon position-premise questions are not re-escalated on anonymous availability alone.

Position read: NVIDIA long's capture thesis weakens slightly in the upside; base street gap stays +2.62 (+0.70%), bull gap narrows +22.78→+19.79. AMD base gap stays approximately zero; no recognized GPU dollars were added.

## 2026-10-12T14:00:30+00:00 — Lease disclosures leave 2027 rack acceptance unresolved; NVIDIA base held at $374.62bn

Run: 6cf21d1f853d44979dbb15cf32b12b43. Item: agent-task-56338d7b, agent-initiated primary power/acceptance follow-up; no new external item.

I found primary buildout windows, but no matched power-ready and rack-acceptance schedule. Microsoft’s FY2026 10-K explicitly warns about power-connection delays; its lease note spans FY2027–33. Alphabet’s Q2 note spans 2026–31 and names a separate Q3 2026 lease commencement. Meta’s July leases are expected to start in 2027–28 [web-454ed8f95a] [web-7e3bfccf0e] [web-7e69fd6db3] [web-b8b374a1b1]. These disclosures predate the channel interviews and independently document infrastructure exposure; they cannot identify its unnamed planner or prove a slip [channel-oct2026].

Amazon’s energy contracts can settle financially instead of delivering electricity when consumption is lower. Their existence does not establish site-level 2027 power readiness [web-c22fb8e0b1]. Alphabet’s lease prepayments also show that cash can precede commencement. Neither lease commitments nor payment maturities are replacement capex guides.

NVIDIA recognizes product revenue when control transfers. The policy supplies no customer-specific acceptance calendar. Its Ohio/OpenAI guarantee disclosure puts the first construction phase in FY2029, so that project cannot substantiate 2027 capacity [web-b93e425ae9] [web-86d7fcc726].

I retain $682.5bn calendar capex, NVIDIA $374.62bn base/$391.79bn bull, Q3 Data Center $103bn and own Q4 $128bn. Move on a dated site or acceptance delay linked to supplier dollars, not a lease total. Late-October customer results and November supplier commentary are the next tests. NVIDIA’s long timing risk is better documented; its base street gap remains +$2.62bn (+0.70%), and AMD’s remains approximately zero.

Investigation: Which primary hyperscaler disclosures provide power-ready dates and shipment/acceptance schedules that could validate or refute the channel’s 2027 deployment constraint? Status: partially answered.

Finding: Identified useful primary windows: Microsoft uncommenced datacenter-heavy leases FY2027–33 and explicit power-connection risk; Alphabet leases 2026–31, a separate Q3 2026 commencement and prepayments before commencement; Meta July leases 2027–28; Amazon annual commitment-payment buckets and energy contracts that may settle financially. None of the reviewed notes supplies a matched site-level power-ready MW, rack shipment/acceptance date and supplier value, so the anonymous 2027 constraint is neither verified nor refuted. NVIDIA product revenue depends on control transfer, with contract-specific acceptance conditions undisclosed. Its Ohio/OpenAI first phase is FY2029, outside calendar 2027; its own engineering leases are not Big Four customer capacity. FY27 Q4 has 14 weeks: own $128bn versus $103bn Q3 is +24.3% total, approximately +15.4% per week assuming a 13-week Q3. Hold every input and the recorded quarters. Disclosure mapping is answered; an actual dated deployment/revenue slip remains unresolved.

What was checked: Corpus searches for power-ready capacity, gigawatts, shipment/acceptance and named Meta projects yielded the channel hypothesis and broad commitments, without a matched site/rack schedule. SEC submissions located the latest pre-cutoff Microsoft FY26 annual, Alphabet/Meta/Amazon Q2 quarterly and NVIDIA annual/Q2 filings. Whole-filing fetch previews returned 600 lines, so FilingSummary.xml identified targeted lease, commitment and accounting-policy HTML pages. Fourteen captured filing/notes excerpts, dates and original URLs are recorded in analysis/2026-10-12-power-sources.json and analysis/power-evidence/. New fetched IDs were not immediately readable through read_source; directly fetched SEC note pages supplied the citable material without inferring absence from a truncated preview. Whole documents and their note pages are the same filing, not separate corroborations.

What was learned: MSFT uncommenced datacenter-heavy leases 329.1 over FY2027–33; GOOGL leases 85.2 over 2026–31 and a separate 5.8 short-term agreement starting Q3 2026; META July leases approximately 68 starting 2027–28, with 18–20-year terms. These are future lease obligations, not annual capex or certified power-ready MW. META contractual amounts due 2026/2027 include third-party cloud and other assets; AMZN's 11.732 uncommenced-lease payment bucket for 2027 is not a commencement schedule. AMZN's derivative-accounted energy subset has long horizons and may settle financially; it does not establish all AWS grid supply or a 2027 shortage. GOOGL H1 prepayments 0.835 demonstrate cash before lease commencement [web-7e3bfccf0e] [web-7e69fd6db3] [web-b8b374a1b1] [web-c22fb8e0b1].

Supplier link: NVIDIA recognition follows transfer of control, not a universally disclosed energization condition. Its specific Ohio SB Energy/OpenAI guarantee milestone is first construction phase FY2029; do not treat that as calendar 2027 capacity. NVIDIA's own engineering/testing leases are not Big Four procurement. FY27 Q4 has 14 weeks: own 128 versus Q3 103 is 24.3% total growth, about 15.4% per week assuming 13-week Q3; the official monthly calendar bridge is preserved [web-b93e425ae9] [web-86d7fcc726] [web-a647365249].

Decision: Hold all forecast inputs and quarters. No replacement company capex guide, measured supplier-share change, or named rack value plus revised acceptance/delivery date was established. Keep the previous channel-based 65.5% NVIDIA bull share; do not add a second haircut for general risk statements predating those interviews. Capex 682.5; NVDA bear/base/bull 351.34/374.62/391.79; AMD base 14.00. Q3 DC 103, own Q4 128, required Q4 129.8645. Forecast moves on matched dated deferrals, revised guides or quantified spend mix.

Verification: analysis/power_follow_up.py validates each contiguous quote against eligible corpus text or the captured SEC excerpt, all unchanged input cells, quarter figures/source IDs and preserved formulas. The workbook SHA-256 is unchanged from the beginning of artifact updates; no model tool mutation was needed. compute agrees with the recorded base and bull. analysis/2026-10-12-power-check.json records the bridge and conditional week-normalized comparisons.

Open: The disclosure map is answered, but anonymous customer identity/order overlap, site power-ready MW, specific rack control-transfer/acceptance terms and affected supplier value remain unresolved. Existing H2 capex, mix/concentration, NVIDIA actuals, AMD GPU and 2027 guide questions are carried forward. Ten questions and their answer dates are in notes/open-questions.md.

Next: no immediate follow-up scheduled; await late-October customer and November supplier disclosures.

Attention: none. No base crossing, >5% change, new contrary position call or analyst-guidance conflict. Prior AMD/Amazon short-premise questions are not re-raised on these general commitment windows.

Position read: NVIDIA timing risk is better documented, but base street gap stays +2.62 (+0.70%), bull +19.79; AMD remains approximately at street. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.
